thread_text:
Nina Park: Quick post-all-hands follow-up on runtime Q&A. Capturing three short clarifying questions about kernel rollout, batching defaults, and cache knobs so we can action.

Priya Desai: Happy to answer. I'll take kernel + cache, Maya can add the timeline details.

Nina Park: Q1: Will kernel-v4 be opt-in or auto-upgraded for hosted customers? Several PMs worried about surprises.

Maya Torres: Opt-in first. Plan: staged canaries in late May, opt-in toggle in Console in June, and a global default flip only after two region canaries and a 72h stability window. No silent auto-upgrades.

Diego Ramos: For Dedicated fleets, do we offer a compatibility shim or rollback path?

Priya Desai: Yes — Dedicated nodes will keep the previous kernel binary for 90 days. We'll also provide an OSS-like compatibility shim that maps KV cache layout when needed. Rollback is a single Console action per-cluster.

Nina Park: Q2: batching defaults — should endpoints use 20ms or 50ms default? We left this ambiguous.

Diego Ramos: Recommendation: `interactive:20ms` (p95-sensitive) and `throughput:50ms` (cost-sensitive). We'll expose both `batch_window_ms` and `batch_target_tokens` in Console presets. Adaptive batching will be opt-in initially.

Nina Park: Q3: cache eviction — customers reported prefixes dropping after short idle times. Any new defaults?

Priya Desai: Moving to segmented LRU with a pinned prefix segment. Defaults: `global_max_entries=100000`, `pinned_ratio=0.03`, `idle_ttl_ms=600000` (10m). Tenants can call `cache.pin=true` on sessions to preserve prefixes.

Maya Torres: Actionables: I'll publish rollout schedule + Console toggle dates by Friday, Priya will add cache API examples to docs, Diego will draft batching recommendation notes.

eng-bot: Created ticket RUNTIME-6601 (publish rollout schedule) and RUNTIME-6602 (cache API docs).

Nina Park: Thanks — once the docs are live I'll add a short note to the all-hands recap. :thumbsup:
